cards.name: Content Credentials (Beta)
cards.summary: Shows the Content Credentials (Beta) panel, where you choose whether Photoshop attaches Content Credentials (C2PA provenance metadata such as the producer's name, connected accounts and a record of edits including generative-AI use) to files it exports. It sets attribution on output and changes no pixels. Enabled with or without a document open; the panel's exact options in 27.4 were not harvested.
use_for: declaring authorship on a portfolio piece or client key visual before export
disclosing generative-AI edits on ad creatives and social posts where a platform or client asks for provenance
attaching a creator name and linked social accounts to images that will circulate online
avoid: deliverables whose spec forbids extra metadata (some ad servers, print RIP workflows): leave credentials off and check the export
using it as copy protection: the metadata is lost on a screenshot or a re-save without it; add a visible watermark if that matters

starting Generative Fill on a selection without going through the Edit menu
hiding the bar when it sits over the area being retouched
avoid: scripted or batch work: call the underlying commands (Select > Subject, Edit > Generative Fill) directly
fine masks of hair or fur: refine the selection in Select and Mask rather than the bar's quick mask

cards.name: Histogram
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Histogram panel, a live graph of how the image's pixels spread from shadows (left) to highlights (right), for the composite, a single channel, luminosity or colours, with optional statistics such as mean, standard deviation, median and pixel count. It only reads the image.
use_for: checking for clipped shadows or blown highlights before a product photo goes to print
watching the tonal range move while adjusting Levels or Curves on a portrait
matching the brightness balance of photos that must sit together in a catalogue or carousel
avoid: reading the colour at one spot: use the Info panel with colour samplers
exact numbers on a large file: the graph may come from the image cache; refresh it to an uncached histogram
cards.script_api: app.runMenuItem(stringIDToTypeID('toggleHistogramPalette')) (verified live 2026-10-04; a second run hid it again). It is a toggle, so check the panel state first. For the numbers in a script read document.histogram (composite) or channel.histogram, arrays of pixel counts per level (both in the PS API harvest; not run).

cards.name: History

taking snapshots of alternative colour grades of a poster during a session
painting an earlier state back into part of a photo with the History Brush
avoid: keeping alternatives after closing the file: history and snapshots are not saved; use Layer Comps or duplicate layers
very long sessions on huge files: many states eat RAM and scratch disk; lower the state count
cards.script_api: app.runMenuItem(stringIDToTypeID('toggleHistoryPalette')) (verified live 2026-10-04; a second run hid it again). It is a toggle, so check the panel state first. To step back by script set document.activeHistoryState = document.historyStates[i] (History and HistoryStates members in the PS API harvest; not run).
